text_summary: Recurring pattern in BAY-2 involving hot work activities near pressure vessels containing H2S-bearing process fluids. When welding or grinding operations occur within 15 metres of vessels V-204B or V-302A during ambient temperatures above 35°C, H2S desorption from micro-leaks at gasket faces increases by 30–60%. Risk is compounded during shift changeover windows when gas-watch continuity is interrupted. Three incidents in the past 18 months share this pattern.

Gas migration through degraded compressor shaft seals has been observed on C-14 when vibration levels exceed 10 mm/s for sustained periods. The failure mode progresses from seal face wear to gas leakage at the seal housing, with migrated gas accumulating in the compressor enclosure. The enclosure's natural ventilation rate is insufficient to disperse gas below 10% LEL when seal leakage exceeds 5 Nm³/h. Pattern links vibration trending data to seal integrity as a leading indicator.

Heat exchangers in BAY-1 operating with shell-side temperature swings greater than 200°C per cycle experience accelerated gasket degradation. HX-110 and HX-503 have both shown micro-cracking after 12–18 months of service when original-specification spiral-wound gaskets are used. The failure mode is gradual bolt-load loss leading to detectable emissions before catastrophic leak. Pattern suggests upgrading to graphite-filled gaskets and reducing inspection intervals from 12 to 6 months for exchangers with ΔT > 200°C.

A 20–30 minute gap in active gas monitoring occurs during shift changeover in BAY-2 when the outgoing gas-watch person stands down before the incoming operator assumes the role. During this window, portable monitors are stored in the control room rather than remaining at the work face. Two of the last four H2S events in BAY-2 occurred within this changeover window. Root cause is procedural — the current shift handover protocol does not mandate continuous gas-watch coverage during transitions.

Overfill risk at T-301 is elevated when the primary level transmitter LT-301A experiences drift during monsoon season (humidity-related moisture ingress). The risk cascades when the independent high-level switch LSHH-301 is simultaneously under maintenance override. Both conditions have coincided once in the past 12 months. The pattern is detectable by cross-referencing the maintenance override log for LSHH-301 against the calibration drift history of LT-301A.

Loss of cooling on R-501 follows a specific cascade: primary pump trip due to low cooling water header pressure, followed by failure of the standby pump to auto-start. Contributing factors include impeller seizure from long standby periods without rotation, and latent faults in the auto-start interlock that are not detected by routine testing. The 2023 fatal incident demonstrated that manual ESD activation adds 3–5 minutes to the response time, during which reactor temperature can exceed the catalyst thermal limit by over 150°C.
